newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council hails Angola's unity government.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council hails Angola's unity government.

text.p: The Security Council welcomed on Friday the inauguration of a national unity government in Angola and said this opened the way for completing other provisions of a peace accord signed in Lusaka, Zambia, in 1994.

The government, whose formation had been repeatedly delayed, includes members of the formerly Marxist Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) and former rebels of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA).
"The council welcomes the inauguration in Angola of the government of unity and national reconciliation," council president Antonio Monteiro of Portugal said in a statement to reporters.

"This is an important step in the Angolan peace process and opens the way for the conclusion of the remaining tasks of the Lusaka protocol and definitive peace, democracy and economic development in Angola," added Monteiro, whose country was Angola's colonial ruler prior to independence in 1975.

A U.N. peacekeeping force of more than 7,000 has been helping implement the peace agreement, including the disarming and demobilization of former UNITA fighters and the incorporation of some of them into a new Angolan army.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan visited Angola last month and helped speed the establishment of the unity government.
